- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent prices are rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is trending upward, model underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior day.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.0% per day from forecast if sentiment is flat or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >10% above model, check if sentiment was bullish; if yes, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment is high and model forecast is low, consider “sentiment lag” — delay adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid overreacting to sentiment spikes.
